result.markdown:
If I were starting a company today, I'd shortlist **ClickUp, Linear, and Notion**\. The best choice depends on whether you're building a tech product, running a general business, or managing a small founding team.

My overall recommendation: **ClickUp for most early-stage startups.**

Here's how I'd compare the options.

## Top 5 project management tools for startups

![The 16 Best Project Management Software Tools In 2024 » Dev Chandra](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/c4VGNA3qY5dnrclvkWa9KMG25irsspA9ISCCWsY3svJkMGgJgdCNFlxPnqL74DlsymMhT2fJruRgHGYS7RSDer2sr0XCWaZKO-Iw6ehZrCbdp7WrzWLfjjLK89jVbecMnmcJ18eYDJft4Q93ZLzuZSQvdnf4oXXEZyxQIKmdu1ke0VTyURcl9o_70rin7uAt?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. ClickUp**

(Best overall)

- Tasks, projects, docs, goals and dashboards.
- Highly customizable.
- Good for managing multiple departments.
- Free plan available.

**Why I'd choose it\:** You can run much of your startup from one platform without buying several different tools.

[Explore ClickUp](https://clickup.com/)

---

![How to Use Linear - Getting Started Guide (2026) | Delv](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/5tofpg1VDIlh8oGcwQv2QUJnntZwOw473tq8b33B9XH_BZ_O4jA0oTtell1c1iXwDaWf75CHFxMUklyWVjhmdspre4n3N4ZKrhPDFYR1PUDfaPVBsCdlbn5mj6rrKv8ntLA6Z4R131DO4ZUYDh3scZWIlIuwWrr80QBgv3PhmIhlW2BJ5g8ZfDqJnCvpyADs?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Linear**

(Best for tech startups)

- Product roadmaps and sprint planning.
- Bug tracking and engineering workflows.
- Excellent developer experience.
- Integrations with GitHub and other developer tools.

**Why I'd choose it\:** If you're building a SaaS product or technology company, it's particularly good for keeping product development focused.

[Explore Linear](https://linear.app/)

---

![Notion | App](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/bJ7hI8ApmaxCv8OOow3tbY1VFo-qGnZa4MmWSLS-58-vvQBrqTTsp2BpGxbMzRmdRInysITvyRWep0iNfaKTtoPE-B_GMcwiAxxvtSBh6ELpSyBgdVSf6DmJdmQhkFxpzfCBn1fpoMKfVK4nenM2ww1_Uw2wXOW6R4NSRPXKbrw8KEtUcXKPcl2IcQGGWaWb?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Notion**

(Best for early-stage teams)

- Project tracking and task databases.
- Company wiki and documentation.
- Meeting notes and strategic planning.
- Product specifications and knowledge management.

**Why I'd choose it\:** Excellent when you're still figuring out your business model, processes and operating procedures.

[Explore Notion](https://www.notion.com/)

---

![BŪP Cards + AI Assistant | Capture Leads and Follow Through](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/7g9IYDS-8l6USub7VHkwyjSLLFnOYWs8FwetK8W9Ww93vNXJGdNXx16hE8UHg12u0WwFl8qV_CDK1uq-XILMyCkv3E1QBTbeUZDChInuE5nsvMDwEzOQo3y-Fcb-bhncJofX6gwd4nKGSw4WpiUUlWtMmrbF6I2BUP2V8aQ_phRTNdo6kKdsPE5N6B0OlJoC?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Asana**

- Excellent task ownership and accountability.
- Project timelines and dependencies.
- Cross-functional collaboration.
- Useful as teams grow.

**Why I'd choose it\:** Great if marketing, operations, sales and product teams need to coordinate.

[Explore Asana](https://asana.com/)

---

**5\. Trello**

- Simple drag-and-drop boards.
- Easy task tracking.
- Very little learning required.
- Good for small teams.

**Why I'd choose it\:** If you want something simple that everyone can start using immediately.

[Explore Trello](https://trello.com/)

## What I'd actually implement

For an early-stage startup, I'd avoid buying too many tools.

I'd start with\:

- **ClickUp\:** All projects, tasks, deadlines and accountability.
- **Notion\:** Company documentation, strategy, meeting notes and SOPs.
- **Slack\:** Team communication.

If you're building a software product, I'd consider replacing ClickUp's engineering workflow with Linear.
